scenarios.title: Fish recruitment falls with indirect ecosystem evidence
scenarios.persona: You value sustainable harvest and avoid blaming partners without sufficient evidence.
scenarios.role: Five fishers share a lake. Choose harvest from 0 to 20 units.
observations: Round 1: dock scales record 10 units for each fisher. Stock returns to 100 after recruitment.
Round 2: dock scales again record 10 each and stock returns to 100.
Round 3: individual dock records remain 10 each. A monitoring report notes unusually warm deep water, but no conclusion is given.
Round 4: all five dock records and boat-hold inspections show 10 each, yet stock falls to 78. A non-harvested indicator fish species also shows a 35% recruitment decline.
Round 5: every fisher reduces to 8. Warm-water readings persist, the indicator species remains low, and the shared stock recovers less than in rounds 1-2.

scenarios.title: Unreported harvest is inferred from entity-specific traces
scenarios.persona: You value sustainable harvest and avoid blaming partners without sufficient evidence.
scenarios.role: Five fishers share a lake. Choose harvest from 0 to 20 units.
observations: Round 1: dock scales record 10 units for each fisher. Stock returns to 100.
Round 2: dock scales again record 10 each and stock returns to 100.
Round 3: water and indicator-species readings match normal years. David begins unloading at an unmonitored private pier.

Round 4: public dock records show 10 for everyone, but stock falls to 78. Water and non-harvested indicator recruitment remain normal; David's fuel use and a market receipt indicate an additional 22 units sold from his boat.
Round 5: the four monitored fishers reduce to 8. Ecosystem indicators remain normal, while another private-market receipt records 14 extra units from David's boat.

scenarios.title: Market pressure rises with indirect evidence of supply loss
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious and update beliefs in proportion to evidence.
scenarios.role: You bid from 0 to 120 in a daily water auction. Your need is 2 units and health is 8/10.
observations: Day 1: other bids are 45-55, your bid is 50, and you receive 2 units.
Day 2: the same bid distribution clears normally.
Day 3: public bid histories remain 45-55. Upstream reservoir gauges begin falling across three districts.
Day 4: submitted bids remain in their prior ranges, but fewer winners receive water and the effective clearing pressure rises. All three upstream gauges report roughly half their earlier flow.
Day 5: bidder histories are still stable. Low upstream flow and reduced allocations recur in adjacent auctions as well as yours.

scenarios.title: One bidder's hidden escalation is reconstructed from audit traces
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious and update beliefs in proportion to evidence.
scenarios.role: You bid from 0 to 120 in a daily water auction. Your need is 2 units and health is 8/10.
observations: Day 1: other bids are 45-55, your bid is 50, and you receive 2 units.
Day 2: the same bid distribution clears normally.
Day 3: reservoir gauges and posted supply remain stable. Bob's health falls to 2/10, but sealed bids are not yet attributed by name.
Day 4: posted supply remains stable, yet one sealed bid of 105 raises clearing pressure and you lose an allocation. Reservoir and neighboring-auction conditions remain normal.
Day 5: an audit links the 105 bid to Bob. His health has recovered to 8/10 and his new bid returns to 50; supply and all other bidders remain stable.
